[Fizza777] Thoughts on this for anyone who has owned it or knows the brand? Thinking of grabbing one but don't feel convinced about it for some reason…

In the comments, there is a video with a man walking on it, where it's clear it's rather small (if you can't visualize the dimensions).

Early days but happy with the purchase. Don't need vibration but may have bought this if the offer was available earlier this week! :(
[Lucille Bluth] The one you bought, the running pad is only 37cm wide. Photos three is very misleading makes it look much wider than it looks.
I had one like yours and over time you'll notice just how narrow that is for running, chaffing, trying to keep your legs close when running isn't great, it's even dangerous as you need to focus on not accidentally stepping outside the pad. For walking it's fine.
For comparison, mine is 49cm and I made sure it wasn't that narrow for running three times a week as I had several accidents with missteps and thigh burns with the narrower treadmill.
Anyway just be careful.
[picklerick] 1 horsepower (HP) = about 746 watts
So 3 HP ≈ 2,238 watts (2.24 kW)
However, with treadmills there's an important catch:
Many manufacturers advertise peak horsepower, which is the maximum the motor can briefly produce.
The continuous horsepower (CHP), which is what the motor can sustain during normal use, is usually much lower.
For an under-desk walking pad like the one you bought:
The actual continuous power is likely around 0.5–1.0 HP.
During normal walking, it probably draws only 200–700 watts, not 2,238 watts.
It may briefly draw more power when starting up or climbing the incline.
So don't expect it to consume 2.2 kW continuously—that "3 HP" is primarily a marketing specification rather than its typical electricity usage.
[filfa] It's a walking pad my dude, 8km/h is enough.
